note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-21). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: This letter is for those who are called, loved by God the Father and kept safe for Jesus Christ: mercy, peace and love to you, more and more.
ideas: An old man reads a handwritten letter at his kitchen table, his hand on his heart
A father's hands tuck a blanket round a child asleep on the sofa
A grandmother takes a child's old drawing out of the box where she has kept it for years
A porch light is left on and a place is laid for the one coming home
A coach calls a boy off the bench with a hand on his shoulder
Cupped hands shelter a seedling from the wind
Tea is poured for a guest until the cup brims over
A girl picked for the team runs into her team-mates' arms
A lighthouse keeper keeps the lamp burning
A postman hands a letter over a garden gate to a woman who has been waiting for it

sections.meaning: Fight for the faith that was handed down once for all, because some have slipped in unnoticed who turn God's grace into a licence to sin.
ideas: A relay runner grips the baton hard as it is passed to her and drives forward
A grandmother closes her granddaughter's fingers round an old family locket
A goalkeeper dives at full stretch to keep the ball out
A shepherd stands between his flock and a prowling dog at dusk
A fox slips under the fence into the hen yard while the farmer's back is turned
A stranger slips in at the back door of a family party, and no one looks up
Bindweed creeps up through a well-built wall
A gardener pulls out the weed that is strangling the roses
A boy told he may take one biscuit empties the whole jar
A night watchman walks the wall with a lantern

sections.meaning: Remember: those who were rescued and then would not trust, and those who left the place given to them, came to ruin. They stand as a warning.
ideas: Walkers roped to a mountain guide cross the snow safely, while two who have unclipped walk off the other way
Rescued hikers are welcomed into the mountain hut, and one turns and walks back out into the blizzard
A fishing boat steers wide of an old wreck on the rocks below the lighthouse
A watchman's post stands empty, the gate wide open, as he walks off toward the lights of town
A burnt forest stands black beside the road as cars pass
A wrecked car is set up beside the road as a warning to drivers
A kite that has snapped its string hangs tangled in a dead tree
A railway carriage lies off the rails beside the track
An empty house with a fallen roof stands on the hill above the village
A father stops with his son on a walk to look at the ruin of a great house

sections.meaning: These people follow their own dreams: they throw off all authority and mock what they do not understand, though even the archangel left the judging to the Lord. Envy, greed and rebellion are an old road to ruin.
ideas: A young deckhand laughs and waves away the old captain who points at the storm ahead
A man drags a road-closed barrier aside and strides onto the broken bridge, ignoring the road worker
A heckler stands and jeers at a doctor explaining an X-ray
A boy scribbles over a master's painting
A big, strong man is shouted at by a smaller furious man and answers nothing, his hands open at his sides
A referee stands calm and silent while a furious player shouts in his face
A man takes a thick envelope in a dim car park, glancing over his shoulder
A well-trodden path, marked by many footprints, runs straight on to a fallen bridge
A crew turns its back on the captain
A sleepwalker walks toward the top of the stairs

sections.meaning: They are all promise and no gift: feeding only themselves, clouds with no rain, trees with no fruit, wild waves, stars that wander off into the dark.
ideas: At a shared meal one man has pulled every dish to himself and eats, while the plates beside him are empty
A jagged rock lurks just under calm blue water in the path of a small boat of laughing friends
A farmer and his son in a cracked, dry field watch a great dark cloud blow past without a drop
In an orchard heavy with apples one bare dead tree lies uprooted
Storm waves throw dirty foam and rubbish up the beach
A shooting star burns out into black sky, away from the steady stars
A shepherd eats his lunch with his back to his thin sheep
An empty well bucket comes up dry
A grand shop window is full of empty boxes
A signpost with its arms broken off stands at a crossroads in the dark

sections.meaning: The Lord is coming with his holy thousands to judge every ungodly deed and every hard word. These are the grumblers and fault-finders, loud boasters who flatter people for gain.
ideas: Everyone in a courtroom rises and turns as the door behind the empty bench opens and light comes through
Morning light cuts into a dark alley, and a man there steps back from it
The hall lights snap on over the mess after a party, and the people in it freeze
A class in uproar freezes as the door handle turns
An inspector's torch lights the cracks hidden behind fresh paint
The tide goes out and shows everything lying on the sea bed
At a table loaded with good food one man scowls and pushes his plate away while everyone else gives thanks
A man fawns on a rich man stepping from his car, laughing too hard and holding the umbrella over him
A man boasts with wide arms to a ring of bored listeners
A child given a present throws it down and points at another

sections.meaning: Remember, you were told this would happen: in the last time mockers come who follow their own desires and split people apart. They do not have the Spirit.
ideas: Two men on a porch laugh and point at a neighbour boarding up his windows under a blue sky, while a storm builds far behind them
At a picnic one man leans in and whispers, and the friends have split into two halves with their backs to each other
A family calmly closes the storm shutters as the storm they were warned of arrives
A farmer who listened has his hay in the barn as the rain begins
A wedge splits a log in two
A crack runs down the middle of a family photograph
Hikers laugh at the ranger's warning and walk on
Two groups of old friends stand at opposite ends of a room with one smirking man between them
An old sailor's warning comes true and the young sailor nods, remembering
A man saws through the branch that a whole row of children's swings hangs from

sections.meaning: But you: build yourselves up on your most holy faith, pray, keep yourselves in God's love and wait for mercy. Be merciful to those who doubt, and snatch others out of the fire, with care.
ideas: A family builds the wall of their house stone by stone on a foundation of solid rock
An old woman keeps a lamp lit at the window, watching the road, with a place laid at the table
Friends keep close round a small fire on a cold night
A bricklayer checks each course with his level
A firefighter drags a dazed man by the arms out of a smoking doorway
A nurse in mask and gloves gently tends a sick man
A man is pulled back by his jacket from the platform edge as the train comes in
A friend sits on the stairs beside a friend full of doubt, an arm round his shoulders
A lifeguard runs into the surf
A woman reaches into a bonfire's edge with tongs to save a child's toy

sections.meaning: He is able to keep you from falling and to bring you, faultless and full of joy, into his glory. To the only God, through Jesus Christ, be glory and power, before all time, now and for ever.
ideas: A father's two hands hold a toddler's raised hands as she walks laughing along a low garden wall
A mountain guide holds the rope firm as a climber crosses a narrow snowy ridge
A friend's arm steadies a blind man across stepping stones
A child on a balance beam holds a steady hand
A family stands small on a hill under a huge sky blazing with stars
Climbers reach the summit at sunrise and throw up their arms above a sea of golden cloud
A bride is walked in, radiant, on her father's arm
A father carries his sleeping child over the threshold into the lit house
A choir sings with faces lifted
The first sun pours over a mountain range

candidates.prompt: At a kitchen table in warm morning light an old man reads a handwritten letter, holding the pages up in one hand with his other hand resting on his heart, his face soft with gladness. A torn-open envelope lies beside his cup. The pages are seen from behind so that no writing shows.

In a living room in the evening a small child of about four lies fast asleep on a sofa. A father's two hands, coming in from the edge of the frame, gently tuck a soft blanket round the child's shoulders. Only the father's hands and forearms are seen. A lamp glows warmly beside the sofa. Peaceful and safe.

On a running track in bright daylight, a close view of a relay handover: one runner's outstretched hand has just passed the baton and a young woman runner grips it hard in her fist, her face set with fierce determination as she drives forward. Her face and the gripped baton are both sharp.

By a window in clear daylight a grandmother places an old gold family locket in her granddaughter's open palm and closes the girl's fingers firmly round it with both her own hands, looking her in the eyes with great seriousness and love. The girl, about twelve, looks back and nods.

In a farmyard in clear morning light a farmer scatters grain to a flock of hens, his back turned. Behind him, unnoticed, a red fox is slipping in under the wire fence, low to the ground, its eyes on the hens. The farmer and hens are calm and unaware. The fox is sharp and clearly seen.

A warm family party in a bright dining room: a dozen relatives laugh and talk round a long table, all facing each other. At the back of the room a stranger in a dark jacket is slipping in quietly through the half-open back door, glancing round. Not one person at the table has noticed him.

On a wide snowfield in clear daylight a mountain guide leads a line of walkers roped together along a safe marked track, looking back with one arm raised in warning. Two walkers have unclipped from the rope and are walking away in the other direction, their backs turned, toward a field of dark open cracks in the ice in the distance.

At the open door of a mountain rescue hut at dusk, in falling snow, exhausted hikers wrapped in blankets are being welcomed into the warm lit room by a rescue team with hot drinks. One rescued hiker, his blanket slipping from his shoulders, has turned his back on the open door and is walking away into the dark blizzard alone. A rescuer in the doorway reaches a hand out after him.

In clear daylight the rusted wreck of an old ship lies broken on dark rocks at the foot of a white lighthouse. A small fishing boat is passing well clear of the rocks, and the two fishermen aboard look across at the wreck soberly, one pointing it out to the other.

At night a watchman's post beside a wide-open gate stands empty: his chair with a lantern still burning on it, his cap left on the seat. The watchman himself, seen from behind, is walking away down the road toward the bright distant lights of a town. Beyond the open, unguarded gate, dark buildings stand unprotected.

On the bridge of a ship in rough grey weather a grey-haired captain points urgently through the window at a huge black storm front ahead, his other hand on the chart. Beside him a young deckhand laughs and waves a hand at him dismissively, leaning back with a careless grin. Both faces are clear.

On a country road in daylight a man is dragging a striped road barrier with flashing lamps out of his way and striding past it toward a bridge whose middle has plainly collapsed into the river. A road worker in a bright jacket holds up both hands to stop him; the man does not even look at him.

On a dockside in daylight a small, furious man shouts up into the face of a very tall, strong dock worker, jabbing a finger at his chest. The big man answers nothing: his mouth is closed, his eyes are calm and steady, and his big hands hang open at his sides. His quiet strength is plain.

On a football pitch in daylight a furious player shouts into the face of a referee from very close, arms flung wide. The referee stands perfectly calm and silent, mouth closed, hands behind his back, looking steadily back at him. Other players watch from behind, out of focus.

In a dim underground car park, lit by one overhead lamp, a man in a good suit takes a thick envelope from another hand that reaches in from the edge of the frame. He is glancing nervously back over his shoulder as he slides it inside his jacket. His face is clearly lit.

A well-worn dirt path, covered with the footprints of many people all going the same way, runs straight ahead across a field to the edge of a deep ravine, where an old footbridge has broken and hangs down into the gap. No fence, no one in sight. Clear daylight.

At a long outdoor table set for a shared meal in daylight, one well-fed man has pulled every dish and basket of food in front of himself and is eating greedily, his arm curled round the food. The plates of the people sitting on either side of him are completely empty, and they look at him in silence.

A calm, bright blue bay on a sunny day, seen from just above the water. In the foreground a dark jagged rock lies just beneath the surface, clearly visible through the clear water. A little way off a small boat full of laughing friends is heading straight toward it, none of them looking at the water.

A farmer and his young son stand in a wide field of cracked, bone-dry earth and withered crops, both looking up with hope fading from their faces as a great dark rain cloud is carried past overhead by the wind. Not a drop is falling; beyond the cloud the sky is already clearing to hard blue.

An orchard in clear autumn daylight, every tree heavy with red apples. In the middle one tree is bare, grey and dead, without a single leaf or fruit, and it lies uprooted on its side with its dry roots in the air. A fruit picker carrying a full basket of apples walks past it.

A wild sea under a dark stormy sky: huge brown-grey waves crash onto a beach and throw up thick dirty yellow foam, and a line of seaweed, driftwood and rubbish is left strewn along the sand. Daylight breaks through one gap in the clouds so the foam is clearly lit.

A night sky over a dark, empty moor. On one side the steady stars shine calmly in their patterns. On the other side a single bright shooting star is streaking away from them, its trail already fading, into a region of sky that is utterly black and starless.

Inside a plain modern courtroom, seen from the back: every person in the room has risen to their feet and stands in silence, all turned toward the front, where the judge's high chair is empty and the door behind it is swinging open with bright light pouring through. No one has come through the door yet. Some stand calmly, one man near the front looks down, afraid.

A narrow city alley at sunrise. The first strong beam of morning sunlight cuts down the length of the alley, lighting up the litter and the walls. A man standing in the alley has thrown an arm up over his eyes and is stepping back from the light into the last patch of shadow. The lit street beyond is bright and clean.

A big family table loaded with a beautiful home-cooked feast in warm daylight. Everyone round the table is smiling, grateful, passing dishes. One man in the middle sits with his arms crossed and a sour scowl, his full plate pushed away from him, pointing at it with a complaint.

On a city pavement a rich man in an expensive coat steps out of a luxury car. Beside him another man bends low, laughing far too eagerly at something he said, holding an umbrella over him and reaching to carry his bag, his eyes fixed on the rich man's face. The rich man does not look at him.

On a sunny street two men sit on a porch with drinks, laughing loudly and pointing across at their neighbour, who is calmly nailing boards over the windows of his house. Far behind them all, low on the horizon, a huge dark storm front is building. The laughing men have not looked behind them.

At a picnic table in a park in daylight a group of eight friends has split in two: four have turned their backs and sit facing one way with hard faces, four the other way. Between the two halves one man leans in to whisper behind his hand into a listener's ear, with a small sly smile.

On a hillside in bright daylight a family, parents and two older children, is building the stone wall of a small house together, lifting and setting each stone carefully on the row below. The wall plainly stands on a broad foundation of solid bare rock. They work gladly, the father passing a stone to his daughter.

At dusk an old woman sits knitting in a chair beside a window with a lit lamp on the sill, lifting her eyes to look out down the empty road with calm, sure hope. Behind her in the warm room a table is laid with an extra place ready. She is waiting for someone who is certainly coming.

A firefighter in full kit, seen from the side, hauls a dazed man in ordinary clothes by both arms out through the doorway of a building pouring thick smoke, with an orange glow deep inside. The rescued man is on his feet, coughing, unhurt. Clear daylight outside lights both their faces.

In a clean, bright hospital isolation room a nurse wearing a mask, gloves and gown bends over a sick man in bed and gently wipes his forehead with a cloth, her eyes above the mask full of kindness. Her careful protective clothing and her tenderness are both plain.

In a sunny garden a toddler of about two walks along the top of a low stone garden wall, laughing, both her small hands held up and firmly gripped by a father's two big hands reaching down from above. Only the father's hands and forearms are seen. She cannot fall.

On a narrow snowy mountain ridge in clear morning light a mountain guide stands braced with the rope held firm in both gloved hands, while the climber roped to him steps surely along the narrowest part of the ridge, smiling, steep drops on either side. The taut rope between them is plainly seen.

A family of four stands on a hilltop at night, seen small and from behind, looking up at an immense sky blazing with thousands of stars and the bright band of the Milky Way. A child points upward. The sky fills most of the picture and is full of light.

Three climbers have just reached a mountain summit at sunrise and throw both arms up with shouts of joy, their faces lit gold. Below and all round them a sea of cloud glows gold and rose in the first sun, with far peaks standing out of it. The sky is vast and full of light.

picks.note: Chosen by eye on 2026-11-21 from the trial pictures, before the chapter was translated. Scenes are written when the recording's timings exist; a pick marked 'if time' is used only if each picture can stay up about 8 seconds.
